metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in late January to assess progress. Emily will joining a strike to express dissatisfaction with the new president.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly agree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from China strongly disagree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 20th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about the joint meeting in late January? I think we should aim for January 20th. What do you think? 

Also, I heard Emily's joining a strike. Is it common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest? I don’t really understand that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think January 20th could work for the meeting. Let's confirm that with everyone. 

About strikes... in China, we don’t really engage in strikes. It’s not a common practice for us. We prefer to resolve issues through dialogue, not protests. Joining a strike seems... unusual to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
That's good to hear about January 20th. I agree, let's confirm with everyone. 

As for strikes, I just find it hard to understand why people would choose that route. In my experience, it's better to have discussions and find solutions instead of joining protests. Doesn’t it seem counterproductive to you?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Yes, it does seem counterproductive. I believe discussions are a much more effective way to address concerns. Strikes can create division and don't lead to constructive outcomes. In our culture, we value harmony and collaboration over conflict. It’s just not how we handle disagreements.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Exactly, I feel the same way. Harmony and collaboration are so important. Strikes just create tension and don’t really solve anything. It’s interesting how different cultures approach these issues. 

So, let’s make sure the January 20th meeting is confirmed. I think it will be a great opportunity to move forward together.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Well, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own ways, you know? At the end of the day, it's all the same. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can work together effectively. 

Now, back to the meeting… confirming January 20th will definitely help us move forward. Let’s get that sorted out.
